_status: UNFUNDED DRAFT. Not posted. Do not post without Oscar.
_written: 2026-10-04 night run, branch night/favour-cleanup-20261004. Revised three times on 2026-10-05 after three cold reads.
_count_note: The brief asked for 10 to 15 favours. 14 were drafted. After three independent reads, 3 remain. The others placed a person in a town, at a spot or at a time, or showed a third party's details, or could not be checked by anything. Fewer good rows beat more risky ones.
_known_limits: Nothing shows that a photo is the sender's own. A picture found online passes as easily as one just taken. The app has no provenance check and this pack does not add one.

The check is a model, not a person. No human reviews a proof on the live app. Each row says what that model can see in the proof and what it cannot. Whether the live model judges these rows well is unverified: none has been posted.

Answers come from one wallet. Several answers from the same wallet add up. That is why no row asks for a town, a spot, a day or a time any more: a town beside photos of real spots, from one wallet, gives a home town and a set of places.

A photo is never placeless. A shelf label or a product pack can still show a chain name, a language, a kitchen counter. The safety clause in each row is an instruction to the sender. Nothing enforces it.

The personal data check that the review test runs is a reviewer's aid. It caught 5 of 20 unsafe asks written after it was frozen and wrongly flagged 3 of 20 safe ones. A green test does not mean a row is safe.

These rows have been read by three cold readers in earlier forms. The current wording of each row, and the whole of label-symbol, has been read by no one but the drafter. A person must read every row before it is posted.
No funder, sponsor or requester exists. Each row would post under a house agent name, which can read as someone wanting the data. Nobody does.
_shape: description, category, points, deadlineHours, maxCompletions, agentId and location are a FavourSpec (src/lib/board-replenish.ts validateFavourSpec). ONLY description reaches the person. safety is a clause that is part of description, repeated here so the review test can find it. The other fields are review notes and are not posted.
_reward_note: points are FAVOUR house points, not money. No sponsor or funder exists for any row, so every row is marked unfunded draft. No row promises a payout.
_demand_note: whoWouldWantIt is a plausible requester, written by the drafter. It is not observed demand. No user asked for these.
_review_note: The review test (src/__tests__/favour-pack.test.ts) is an aid. Its personal data check is a pattern matcher that caught 5 of 20 unsafe asks written after it was frozen, and wrongly flagged 3 of 20 safe ones. A green test does not mean a row is safe. A person must read every row before it is posted.

_dropped.why: the street outside plus the town is a view from home for most people
a speed test screenshot often shows IP address and provider
a financial screen, and photographing one can cause trouble for the person
a photo carries other people's names and numbers, and the words-only version could not be checked
an opinion in text that nothing can check
text only and not checkable; a photo version would mean photographing a toilet entrance
a town, a day and a time beside a photo of a real spot, and a pharmacy sign can name the pharmacist on duty
a photo of a real public spot beside a town, and 'or say it is dry' is a word the photo cannot show
a departure board shows the station and the time: it places a person in space and time
a named kind of building in a town is a real spot, people stand at entrances, and the answer is a judgement
a poster can carry an organiser's name and phone number, and it dates and places the sender
History differs for each person, so nothing can check the answer against the sender's screen, and the live check is a model
a menu board is a named place in a town
a photo of a real public spot beside a town

favours.description: Photo the shelf price labels for a litre of milk and a loaf of bread in a shop. Name the country. Labels only: no people, no receipts, no shop sign.
favours.safety: Labels only: no people, no receipts, no shop sign.
favours.checkedBy: the live model check, not a person
favours.proofShows: Two shelf labels with prices and a currency that can be read.
favours.proofCannotShow: Who took the photo. Nothing shows it is the sender's own and not one found online. Not when it was taken, and not that it is from the country named. A label can carry a chain name; the clause asks to leave the shop sign out and nothing enforces it.
favours.proofRequired: One or two photos with both shelf labels readable. Note: the country only. The first versions asked for the town; a town beside a photo of a real shop, from one wallet, placed the person.
favours.whoWouldWantIt: Anyone comparing the cost of living between countries. A person about to move. A price tracker that has no shelf data.

favours.description: Translate this line into another language you speak, and name the language. The line: "Show your proof, earn your points." Nothing about you is needed.
favours.proofKind: text the model can check against the posted line
favours.checkedBy: the live model check, not a person
favours.proofShows: Whether the text is a fair translation of the posted line into the language named. A multilingual model can judge that from the two texts alone.
favours.proofCannotShow: That the sender speaks the language or wrote it: a machine translation passes. Naming a language is a small fact about the sender, and the ask says another language you speak, not the one spoken at home. Whether the live model check judges this well is unverified.
favours.proofRequired: A text answer: the translated line and the name of the language.
favours.whoWouldWantIt: The FAVOUR team, for a first translated screen. Live answers on 4 Oct came in Spanish, Indonesian, Tagalog and Japanese (source: raw/api_tasks.json proof notes).

favours.description: Photo a warning or sorting symbol on the pack of a product sold in your country. Say what the symbol means. Pack only: no people, no receipts, no addresses.
favours.safety: Pack only: no people, no receipts, no addresses.
favours.checkedBy: the live model check, not a person
favours.proofShows: A product pack with a printed symbol that can be seen, and a stated meaning the model can compare with the symbol.
favours.proofCannotShow: Who took the photo. Nothing shows it is the sender's own and not one found online. Not that the product is sold in the sender's country. A pack on a kitchen counter shows a little of a home; the clause cannot prevent that.
favours.proofRequired: One photo of the symbol on a product pack. Note: what it means. No country is asked for in words beyond the product being sold there. NEW in the third revision and read by no one but the drafter.
favours.whoWouldWantIt: A visitor or new resident who cannot read what a symbol on a pack is telling them to do. Plausible, not observed.
